evidence: Cic. Div. 2.55: nōn numquam etiam errōrem creat similitūdō
terms.comment: Of nature or a place producing something, and of causing: errōrem, lītēs, moram creāre (Lewis & Short). In Christian Latin, of God’s creating (Gen. 1.1). Classically it is also to elect a magistrate: cōnsulēs creāre.

evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.23: fingere et cōnstruere nīdōs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of shaping something with the hands, or in the mind.
Of founding a city, a people, an institution.

phrases.latin: nōn numquam etiam errōrem creat similitūdō
phrases.english: sometimes, too, a likeness creates confusion

phrases.latin: In prīncipiō creāvit Deus caelum et terram.
phrases.english: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.

sources: Lewis & Short: creo · Lewis & Short: fingo · Lewis & Short: condo
